# Slack Web API Reference

Reference for interacting with the Slack Web API through this skill. Read this file when an operation is not covered by a bundled script, or when you need scope, endpoint, rate-limit, or error details.

## Table of Contents

1. [Authentication](#authentication)
2. [Scopes](#scopes)
3. [Endpoints](#endpoints)
4. [Rate Limits](#rate-limits)
5. [Error Handling](#error-handling)
6. [Message Formatting (mrkdwn)](#message-formatting-mrkdwn)
7. [Pagination](#pagination)
8. [Calling the API Directly](#calling-the-api-directly)

## Authentication

- Bot tokens look like `xoxb-...`; send them as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
- Base URL: `https://slack.com`. All responses are JSON with an `ok` boolean. When `ok` is `false`, an `error` string explains why.
- Use the `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` environment variable or the `--token` flag; never hard-code tokens in commands or files.

## Scopes

| Operation | Endpoint | Required scopes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Post message | chat.postMessage | chat:write |
| Reply in thread | chat.postMessage with `thread_ts` | chat:write |
| Post ephemeral message | chat.postEphemeral | chat:write |
| List conversations | conversations.list | channels:read, groups:read, im:read, mpim:read |
| Read channel history | conversations.history | channels:history |
| Read thread replies | conversations.replies | channels:history |
| Search messages | search.messages | search:read |
| List users | users.list | users:read |
| Get user info | users.info | users:read |
| Add/remove reaction | reactions.add / reactions.remove | reactions:write |
| Upload file | files.upload | files:write |

## Endpoints

### chat.postMessage

`POST /api/chat.postMessage`

Body: `{ "channel": "C...", "text": "...", "thread_ts": "...", "mrkdwn": true, "link_names": true }`

- `text` is required unless `blocks` (Block Kit) is provided.
- `thread_ts` posts a reply inside that thread.
- Response: `{ ok: true, channel, ts, message: {...} }`. The `ts` value identifies the message; reuse it as `thread_ts` or in URLs.

### conversations.list

`GET /api/conversations.list?types=public_channel,private_channel,im,mpim&limit=200&cursor=...`

- `types` defaults to `public_channel,private_channel`.
- Results include `is_archived`, `is_private`, `is_member`, `num_members`.

### conversations.history

`GET /api/conversations.history?channel=C...&limit=100&cursor=...`

- `oldest` / `latest` accept Unix timestamps like `"1720000000.123456"`.
- For thread replies use `conversations.replies` with `channel` and `ts`.

### search.messages

`GET /api/search.messages?query=...&count=20&cursor=...`

- Query syntax: `from:@alice`, `in:#general`, `before:2024-01-01`, `after:2024-01-01`, quoted phrases `"exact phrase"`.
- Response: `messages.matches[]` with `channel`, `ts`, `user`, `text`, `permalink`; `messages.total` is the match count.

### users.list

`GET /api/users.list?limit=200&cursor=...`

- Members include bots (`is_bot: true`) and deleted users (`deleted: true`).

### files.upload

`POST /api/files.upload` (multipart/form-data)

- Fields: `channels` (comma-separated), `file` (binary), `filename`, `initial_comment`.

## Rate Limits

- Slack limits each method per workspace per minute by "tier". Most chat/read methods are Tier 3 (~50 req/min); `users.list` and `conversations.list` are Tier 2 (~20 req/min).
- On limit, Slack returns HTTP 429 with a `Retry-After` header in seconds. Back off by that amount; do not retry immediately.

## Error Handling

Always check `ok`. When `false`, the `error` field contains the reason. Common errors:

| error | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| invalid_auth | Token is invalid or expired |
| missing_scope | Token lacks the required scope |
| not_authorized | Token cannot access that resource |
| channel_not_found | Bad channel ID, or the bot is not a member of the channel |
| is_archived | Channel is archived |
| ratelimited | Too many requests; back off per `Retry-After` |
| invalid_ts | Bad `ts` / `thread_ts` value |
| user_not_found | Bad user ID |

## Message Formatting (mrkdwn)

- `*bold*`, `_italic_`, `~strike~`, `` `code` ``, triple-backtick code blocks
- `>quote` for blockquotes
- `@user` and `#channel` mentions require `link_names: true` in the payload to resolve
- Links: `<https://example.com|Link text>`
- Emoji: `:tada:`
- Rich layouts (buttons, sections) use Block Kit `blocks`; see <https://api.slack.com/reference/block-kit/blocks>

## Pagination

List/history/search endpoints return `response_metadata.next_cursor` when more results exist. Repeat the request with `cursor=<value>` until it is empty. The bundled scripts accept `--cursor`.

## Calling the API Directly

With the bundled helper:

```bash
node scripts/slack_request.cjs POST /api/chat.postMessage --data '{"channel":"C...","text":"hi"}'
```

With curl:

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_BOT_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"channel":"C...","text":"hi"}'
```

Use `--dry-run` on the helper to preview the request before sending.

Use when Gemini CLI needs to send or retrieve Slack messages, reply in threads, list workspace channels or users, or find messages on behalf of a Slack bot or app.

# Slack API

## Overview

Send and read Slack messages through the Slack Web API using a bot token. The scripts in `scripts/` wrap the most common operations; `references/slack-api.md` documents endpoints, scopes, rate limits, and error handling for operations without a dedicated script.

## Prerequisites

- A Slack bot token (`xoxb-...`) with the scopes for the operation. Scope table: [references/slack-api.md](references/slack-api.md).
- Provide the token via the `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` environment variable (preferred) or `--token <token>`. Never hard-code tokens.
- Node.js 18+ (scripts use the built-in `fetch`).

## Quick Start

Post a message to a channel:

```bash
SLACK_BOT_TOKEN=xoxb-... node scripts/post_message.cjs --channel C0123456789 --text "Hello from Gemini CLI!"
```

Preview any request before sending it with `--dry-run`:

```bash
node scripts/post_message.cjs --channel C0123456789 --text "Hello" --dry-run
```

## Choosing an Operation

| User wants to... | Use |
| --- | --- |
| Send a message or reply in a thread | `scripts/post_message.cjs` |
| List channels/DMs in the workspace | `scripts/list_conversations.cjs` |
| Read recent messages in a channel | `scripts/fetch_history.cjs` |
| Find messages across the workspace | `scripts/search_messages.cjs` |
| Look up workspace users | `scripts/list_users.cjs` |
| Something else (reactions, files, ephemeral messages, ...) | Call the API directly per [references/slack-api.md](references/slack-api.md) |

## Post Messages

`scripts/post_message.cjs` posts with `chat.postMessage`. Options:

- `--channel <id-or-name>` (required)
- `--text <text>` (required)
- `--thread-ts <ts>`: reply inside a thread instead of the channel
- `--token <token>`, `--dry-run`

```bash
node scripts/post_message.cjs --channel general --text "Deploy finished: all green" --thread-ts 1720000000.123456
```

On success it prints the message `ts` and channel ID.

**Formatting:** Slack uses mrkdwn, not Markdown: `*bold*`, `_italic_`, `` `code` ``, `>quote`, `<https://example.com|Link text>`. Convert user-facing Markdown to mrkdwn before sending. Details: [Message Formatting](references/slack-api.md#message-formatting-mrkdwn).

## Read Messages

`scripts/fetch_history.cjs` reads recent messages (`conversations.history`):

```bash
node scripts/fetch_history.cjs --channel general --limit 20
```

`scripts/search_messages.cjs` searches the whole workspace (`search.messages`):

```bash
node scripts/search_messages.cjs --query "deploy failed in:#general"
```

Both print pagination cursors when more results exist; pass them back with `--cursor`.

## List Channels and Users

```bash
node scripts/list_conversations.cjs --types public_channel,private_channel,im,mpim
node scripts/list_users.cjs
```

## API Calls Without a Script

For endpoints without a script (reactions, files, user groups, etc.), use the helper or curl. Pattern and endpoint reference: [references/slack-api.md](references/slack-api.md).

```bash
node scripts/slack_request.cjs POST /api/reactions.add --data '{"channel":"C0123456789","name":"thumbsup","timestamp":"1720000000.123456"}'
```

## Working with Results

- All scripts print clean, truncated, line-oriented output; exit code 0 on success, 1 on failure.
- Always check for `Failure:` output before assuming an operation succeeded.
- On `ratelimited` / HTTP 429, back off using the printed `Retry-After` value and retry once.

Triggers include "send a Slack message", "post to #channel", "read Slack history", "find a Slack message", or any request to call Slack API methods such as chat.postMessage, conversations.list, conversations.history, search.messages, or users.list.

# Slack API

Interact with a Slack workspace through the Slack Web API.

## Prerequisites

- A Slack bot token (`xoxb-...`) or user token (`xoxp-...`) available as the environment variable `SLACK_TOKEN`.
- The token must have the scopes required by the method being called. Common scopes: `chat:write` (posting), `channels:read`/`groups:read` (conversations.list), `channels:history`/`groups:history` (history), `search:read` (search), `users:read` (users.list).
- If no token is present, ask the user how they want to provide it (env var, file, or inline value). Never hardcode a token in source files.

## Core pattern

Every Slack Web API call uses the same HTTP pattern:

- Endpoint: `https://slack.com/api/<method>`
- Auth header: `Authorization: Bearer <SLACK_TOKEN>`
- Body: `application/json; charset=utf-8` JSON, or `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` for form params
- Response is always JSON. Check `ok` first: `{"ok": true, ...}` on success; `{"ok": false, "error": "..."}` on failure.

Important behavior notes:

- `conversations.*` methods cover both public channels and private channels/groups/DMs (depending on scopes); do not assume the old `channels.*`/`groups.*` methods exist for all token types.
- `conversations.list` is paginated (cursor + `response_metadata.next_cursor`); fetch all pages when a complete list is needed.
- Rate limits apply per method tier; on `ratelimited` responses, wait for the `Retry-After` header seconds before retrying.
- Timestamps in history are Unix epoch seconds (floating point, e.g. `1710000000.123456`); do not treat them as milliseconds.
- To resolve a channel name like `#general` to an ID, call `conversations.list` (or `conversations.info` if the ID is known) and match `name`. Posting requires the channel **ID**, not the name.

## Common operations

### 1. Post a message

Call `chat.postMessage` with `channel` (channel ID), `text`, and optionally `thread_ts` to reply in a thread. Keep messages concise; do not fabricate confirmation that a message was delivered — verify `ok: true` in the response.

Example request body:

```json
{"channel": "C1234567890", "text": "Hello from Gemini CLI"}
```

### 2. List conversations

Call `conversations.list` with `types` (e.g., `public_channel,private_channel`) and `limit` (default 100, max 1000). Iterate `response_metadata.next_cursor` until empty to get all conversations. Each item has `id`, `name`, `is_channel`, `is_private`, `is_member`.

### 3. Fetch channel history

Call `conversations.history` with `channel` and optional `limit`, `oldest`/`latest` (Unix epoch seconds), and `inclusive`. Returns `messages` (newest first) and `has_more`. To read the full history, paginate with `cursor` until `has_more` is false.

### 4. Search messages

Call `search.messages` with `query` (Slack search syntax, e.g., `from:@alice in:#general`). Returns `messages.matches` with `text`, `channel`, `ts`, and `permalink`. Requires `search:read` scope.

### 5. List users

Call `users.list` with `limit` and paginate with `cursor`. Each user has `id`, `name`, `real_name`, and `profile.email`. To resolve a display name or email to a user ID, match on `name`, `real_name`, or `profile.email`.

## Scripts

Reusable Node.js scripts are provided under `scripts/` and must be run with the `SLACK_TOKEN` environment variable set. They print concise, LLM-friendly output (never raw JSON dumps) and exit non-zero on API errors:

- `scripts/slack_request.cjs` — generic authenticated GET/POST wrapper for any method; pass method, params, and optional HTTP verb.
- `scripts/post_message.cjs` — post a message: `node post_message.cjs <channel-id> <text> [thread_ts]`.
- `scripts/list_conversations.cjs` — list conversations (optionally filtered by name substring): `node list_conversations.cjs [name-filter]`.
- `scripts/fetch_history.cjs` — fetch recent history: `node fetch_history.cjs <channel-id> [limit]`.
- `scripts/search_messages.cjs` — search: `node search_messages.cjs "<query>"`.
- `scripts/list_users.cjs` — list users: `node list_users.cjs [name-filter]`.

Prefer these scripts over ad-hoc inline code for deterministic calls. Inspect a script with `read_file` before patching or adapting it.

## References

See `references/slack-api.md` for the full method reference: parameter tables, error codes (e.g., `not_in_channel`, `invalid_auth`, `missing_scope`, `ratelimited`), pagination details, and Slack search query syntax. Read it when the task needs a method not covered above, when debugging a specific error, or when constructing complex search queries.

```bash
node scripts/search_messages.cjs --query "deploy failed in:#general"
```

Both print pagination cursors when more results exist; pass them back with `--cursor`.

## List Channels and Users

```bash
node scripts/list_conversations.cjs --types public_channel,private_channel,im,mpim
node scripts/list_users.cjs
```

## API Calls Without a Script

For endpoints without a script (reactions, files, user groups, etc.), use the helper or curl. Pattern and endpoint reference: [references/slack-api.md](references/slack-api.md).

```bash
node scripts/slack_request.cjs POST /api/reactions.add --data '{"channel":"C0123456789","name":"thumbsup","timestamp":"1720000000.123456"}'
```

## Working with Results

- All scripts print clean, truncated, line-oriented output; exit code 0 on success, 1 on failure.
- Always check for `Failure:` output before assuming an operation succeeded.
- On `ratelimited` / HTTP 429, back off using the printed `Retry-After` value and retry once.

# Slack API

Interact with a Slack workspace through the Slack Web API.

## Prerequisites

- A Slack bot token (`xoxb-...`) or user token (`xoxp-...`) available as the environment variable `SLACK_TOKEN`.
- The token must have the scopes required by the method being called. Common scopes: `chat:write` (posting), `channels:read`/`groups:read` (conversations.list), `channels:history`/`groups:history` (history), `search:read` (search), `users:read` (users.list).
- If no token is present, ask the user how they want to provide it (env var, file, or inline value). Never hardcode a token in source files.

## Core pattern

Every Slack Web API call uses the same HTTP pattern:

- Endpoint: `https://slack.com/api/<method>`
- Auth header: `Authorization: Bearer <SLACK_TOKEN>`
- Body: `application/json; charset=utf-8` JSON, or `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` for form params
- Response is always JSON. Check `ok` first: `{"ok": true, ...}` on success; `{"ok": false, "error": "..."}` on failure.

Important behavior notes:

- `conversations.*` methods cover both public channels and private channels/groups/DMs (depending on scopes); do not assume the old `channels.*`/`groups.*` methods exist for all token types.
- `conversations.list` is paginated (cursor + `response_metadata.next_cursor`); fetch all pages when a complete list is needed.
- Rate limits apply per method tier; on `ratelimited` responses, wait for the `Retry-After` header seconds before retrying.
- Timestamps in history are Unix epoch seconds (floating point, e.g. `1710000000.123456`); do not treat them as milliseconds.
- To resolve a channel name like `#general` to an ID, call `conversations.list` (or `conversations.info` if the ID is known) and match `name`. Posting requires the channel **ID**, not the name.

## Common operations

### 1. Post a message

Call `chat.postMessage` with `channel` (channel ID), `text`, and optionally `thread_ts` to reply in a thread. Keep messages concise; do not fabricate confirmation that a message was delivered — verify `ok: true` in the response.

Example request body:

```json
{"channel": "C1234567890", "text": "Hello from Gemini CLI"}
```

### 2. List conversations

Call `conversations.list` with `types` (e.g., `public_channel,private_channel`) and `limit` (default 100, max 1000). Iterate `response_metadata.next_cursor` until empty to get all conversations. Each item has `id`, `name`, `is_channel`, `is_private`, `is_member`.

### 3. Fetch channel history

Call `conversations.history` with `channel` and optional `limit`, `oldest`/`latest` (Unix epoch seconds), and `inclusive`. Returns `messages` (newest first) and `has_more`. To read the full history, paginate with `cursor` until `has_more` is false.

### 4. Search messages

Call `search.messages` with `query` (Slack search syntax, e.g., `from:@alice in:#general`). Returns `messages.matches` with `text`, `channel`, `ts`, and `permalink`. Requires `search:read` scope.

### 5. List users

Call `users.list` with `limit` and paginate with `cursor`. Each user has `id`, `name`, `real_name`, and `profile.email`. To resolve a display name or email to a user ID, match on `name`, `real_name`, or `profile.email`.

## Scripts

Reusable Node.js scripts are provided under `scripts/` and must be run with the `SLACK_TOKEN` environment variable set. They print concise, LLM-friendly output (never raw JSON dumps) and exit non-zero on API errors:

- `scripts/slack_request.cjs` — generic authenticated GET/POST wrapper for any method; pass method, params, and optional HTTP verb.
- `scripts/post_message.cjs` — post a message: `node post_message.cjs <channel-id> <text> [thread_ts]`.
- `scripts/list_conversations.cjs` — list conversations (optionally filtered by name substring): `node list_conversations.cjs [name-filter]`.
- `scripts/fetch_history.cjs` — fetch recent history: `node fetch_history.cjs <channel-id> [limit]`.
- `scripts/search_messages.cjs` — search: `node search_messages.cjs "<query>"`.
- `scripts/list_users.cjs` — list users: `node list_users.cjs [name-filter]`.

Prefer these scripts over ad-hoc inline code for deterministic calls. Inspect a script with `read_file` before patching or adapting it.

## References

See `references/slack-api.md` for the full method reference: parameter tables, error codes (e.g., `not_in_channel`, `invalid_auth`, `missing_scope`, `ratelimited`), pagination details, and Slack search query syntax. Read it when the task needs a method not covered above, when debugging a specific error, or when constructing complex search queries.
